examples.text: The professor gave an erudite lecture that impressed everyone in the audience.
His erudite knowledge of ancient history made him a sought-after speaker.
She was praised for her erudite contributions to the academic journal.
At all events, if it involved any secret information in regard to old Roger Chillingworth, it was in a tongue unknown to the erudite clergyman, and did but increase the bewilderment of his mind.

examples.text: The volcano erupted, spewing lava across a wide area.

examples.text: The third molar tooth erupts late in most people, and sometimes does not appear at all.

raw_glosses: (intransitive) To burst forth; to break out.

examples.text: The whole table erupted in laughter.
And Stamford Bridge erupted with joy as Florent Malouda slotted in a cross from Drogba, who had stayed just onside.

examples.text: Some of the most beautiful and thus appealing physical theories, including quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravity, have been dogged for decades by infinities that erupt when theorists try to prod their calculations into new domains. Getting rid of these nagging infinities has probably occupied far more effort than was spent in originating the theories.
